sampleLines: ALEC had fresh news in our sources. On October 5, Alector disclosed a September 30 license agreement with Genentech for certain GCase candidates: Genentech leads development and commercialization, Alector keeps its Brain Carrier platform and wholly owned pipeline, and the company said the deal extends its cash runway into 2029. No upfront, milestone or deal-value terms were given.

On October 6, Robo.ai reported September revenue above US$100 million and said it expected about US$600 million of revenue for 2026. No audited statement in our sources supported the September figure.

On October 6, 60 Degrees Pharmaceuticals said it intended to conclude enrollment at 30 subjects in its severe-babesiosis tafenoquine study, unblind it, report primary and secondary endpoint results in January 2027, and request a pre-sNDA meeting with the FDA that month. No endpoint results were disclosed.

On October 6, Locafy reported in a 6-K a definitive agreement to acquire Map Labs' assets and customer base for up to $3.0 million in cash, $2.0 million up front and up to $1.0 million tied to performance. The company expects about $2.0 million in ARR and about $900,000 in 2026 EBIT from the business, subject to closing conditions, and no closing date was given.

The latest news we found was from October 4: at its first annual Las Vegas conference, AIFA said two Teach OS modules were live, four more were in development, and a formal launch was expected in the near term. No revenue, customer or date figures were given.

The latest company news we found was shareholder approval, announced August 25, of the all-stock merger of Olin and Huntsman, a step toward completion and not a close. On October 1, Wells Fargo kept its Equal-Weight rating and lowered its target to $16.
